newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: ALPINE SKIING-SYKORA TAKES LEAD IN WORLD CUP SLALOM.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-SYKORA TAKES LEAD IN WORLD CUP SLALOM.

text.p: In-form Austrian Thomas Sykora took the lead after the first leg of the classic men's World Cup slalom in Kitzbuehel on Sunday, ahead of two compatriots.
Sykora, who recorded his maiden World Cup victory at last year's edition of the race, clocked a best descent time of 46.86 seconds on the Ganslern piste, flagged with 55 gates.
He was 0.17 seconds ahead of 1996 world championship slalom silver medallist Mario Reiter and 0.19 ahead of defending Olympic slalom champion Thomas Stangassinger.
The 28-year old Sykora has been the dominant figure in slalom this season, winning five of the six races staged so far and finishing second in the other.
Sykora could secure the slalom World Cup trophy here if he wins and his only remaining rival in this fight, Stangassinger, finishes worse than 12th.

He would become only the second Austrian to clinch the slalom title since the World Cup circuit began in 1967. Only Austria's Alfred Matt managed the deed in the 1969 and he shared the trophy with three Frenchmen -- Jean Noel Augert, Patrick Russel and Alain Penz.
Norway's Finn Christian Jagge was fourth in 47.12 after the first run, ahead of Italian Olympic and world champion Alberto Tomba in 47.56 and Slovenia's Jure Kosir with 47.62.
Last year's World Cup slalom champion Sebastien Amiez of France crashed out on the upper part of the course.
The second run was scheduled to start at 1230 GMT.
